review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

2:1.sourceText: Καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ γάμος ἐγένετο ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἦν ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐκεῖ·
2:1.targetText: On the third day a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there,

groups.note: The dative of time ἡμέρᾳ supplies On.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:2.sourceText: ἐκλήθη δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν γάμον.
2:2.targetText: and Jesus and His disciples had also been invited to the wedding.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:3.sourceText: καὶ ὑστερήσαντος οἴνου λέγει ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν Οἶνον οὐκ ἔχουσιν.
2:3.targetText: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to Him, “They have no more wine.”

groups.note: The genitive absolute ὑστερήσαντος οἴνου ("the wine having run short") is rendered as a when-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:4.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, γύναι; οὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα μου.
2:4.targetText: “Woman, why does this concern us?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”

groups.note: The idiom Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ("what to me and to you?") is rendered why does this concern us.

studyHeads.note: ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ("to me and to you") together are rendered us.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῇ ("to her") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English verbalizes the idiom; the Greek has no verb.

2:5.sourceText: λέγει ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ τοῖς διακόνοις Ὅ τι ἂν λέγῃ ὑμῖν, ποιήσατε.
2:5.targetText: His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever He tells you.”

groups.note: The dative τοῖς διακόνοις supplies to.
Ὅ τι ἄν ("whatever") works as one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:6.sourceText: ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ λίθιναι ὑδρίαι ἓξ κατὰ τὸν καθαρισμὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων κείμεναι, χωροῦσαι ἀνὰ μετρητὰς δύο ἢ τρεῖς.
2:6.targetText: Now six stone water jars had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification. Each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons.

groups.note: Distributive ἀνά ("apiece") is rendered Each.
μετρητὰς δύο ἢ τρεῖς ("two or three measures") is converted to gallons.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:7.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Γεμίσατε τὰς ὑδρίας ὕδατος. καὶ ἐγέμισαν αὐτὰς ἕως ἄνω.
2:7.targetText: Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.”  So they filled them to the brim.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῖς ("them") is rendered the servants.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:8.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἀντλήσατε νῦν καὶ φέρετε τῷ ἀρχιτρικλίνῳ. οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν.
2:8.targetText: “Now draw some out,” He said, “and take it to the master of the banquet.”  They did so,

groups.note: The dative τῷ ἀρχιτρικλίνῳ supplies to.
In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.
ἤνεγκαν ("they brought it") is rendered did so.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB leaves the addressees αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; Ἀντλήσατε has none in Greek.
English supplies an object; φέρετε has none in Greek.

2:9.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐγεύσατο ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον γεγενημένον, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει πόθεν ἐστίν, οἱ δὲ διάκονοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ ἠντληκότες τὸ ὕδωρ, φωνεῖ τὸν νυμφίον ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος
2:9.targetText: and the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine. He did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside

groups.note: BSB makes the ὡς ("when") clause a main sentence and marks the sequence with Then.
πόθεν means "from where".
The repeated ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος ("the master of the banquet") is rendered he.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

2:10.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος πρῶτον τὸν καλὸν οἶνον τίθησιν, καὶ ὅταν μεθυσθῶσιν τὸν ἐλάσσω· σὺ τετήρηκας τὸν καλὸν οἶνον ἕως ἄρτι.
2:10.targetText: and said, “Everyone serves the fine wine first, and then the cheap wine after the guests are drunk. But you have saved the fine wine until now!”

groups.note: Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ("every man") is rendered Everyone.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.
English marks the contrast; the Greek has no connective here.

2:11.sourceText: Ταύτην ἐποίησεν ἀρχὴν τῶν σημείων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐφανέρωσεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
2:11.targetText: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee. He thus revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.

groups.note: The article τῶν is rendered as the possessive His.
BSB renders this καί as thus, marking the result.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:12.sourceText: Μετὰ τοῦτο κατέβη εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκεῖ ἔμειναν οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας.
2:12.targetText: After this, He went down to Capernaum with His mother and brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there a few days.

groups.note: αὐτὸς καί ("He and") is rendered He … with.
οὐ πολλάς ("not many") is rendered a few.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:13.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
2:13.targetText: When the Jewish Passover was near, Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

groups.note: BSB subordinates the first clause; the καί joining the two clauses is rendered When.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:14.sourceText: καὶ εὗρεν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τοὺς πωλοῦντας βόας καὶ πρόβατα καὶ περιστερὰς καὶ τοὺς κερματιστὰς καθημένους,
2:14.targetText: In the temple courts He found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables.

groups.note: The article with the participle πωλοῦντας ("the ones selling") is rendered men selling.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The καί is not expressed; BSB lists the items with commas.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds where they sat; the Greek has only the participle καθημένους ("sitting").

2:15.sourceText: καὶ ποιήσας φραγέλλιον ἐκ σχοινίων πάντας ἐξέβαλεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ τά τε πρόβατα καὶ τοὺς βόας, καὶ τῶν κολλυβιστῶν ἐξέχεεν τὰ κέρματα καὶ τὰς τραπέζας ἀνέτρεψεν,
2:15.targetText: So He made a whip out of cords and drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle. He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables.

groups.note: The participle ποιήσας ("having made") is rendered as the finite verb made.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ποιήσας is rendered as the finite verb made.

2:16.sourceText: καὶ τοῖς τὰς περιστερὰς πωλοῦσιν εἶπεν Ἄρατε ταῦτα ἐντεῦθεν, μὴ ποιεῖτε τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Πατρός μου οἶκον ἐμπορίου.
2:16.targetText: To those selling doves He said, “Get these out of here! How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!”

groups.note: The article τοῖς with the participle πωλοῦσιν ("to the ones selling") is rendered To those selling.
The prohibitive μή ("do not") is rendered as the rebuke How dare.
οἶκον ἐμπορίου ("a house of trade") is rendered a marketplace; into marks what the house is turned into.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:17.sourceText: ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι γεγραμμένον ἐστίν Ὁ ζῆλος τοῦ οἴκου σου καταφάγεταί με.
2:17.targetText: His disciples remembered that it is written: “Zeal for Your house will consume Me.”

groups.note: The genitive τοῦ οἴκου ("of the house") names the object of zeal and is rendered for … house.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:18.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Τί σημεῖον δεικνύεις ἡμῖν, ὅτι ταῦτα ποιεῖς;
2:18.targetText: On account of this, the Jews demanded, “What sign can You show us to prove Your authority to do these things?”

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν ("answered and said") is condensed to demanded.
The finite ποιεῖς ("You do") is rendered as the infinitive to do.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῷ ("to Him") unexpressed.
BSB recasts the ὅτι clause ("seeing that You do these things") as a request for proof of authority.

unmappedTarget.reason: English paraphrases what the sign must show; the Greek has no verb prove or noun authority.

2:19.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον, καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν.
2:19.targetText: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.”

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is condensed to answered.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (to them) after answered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds again for the rebuilding; ἐγερῶ is simply "I will raise".

2:20.sourceText: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Τεσσεράκοντα καὶ ἓξ ἔτεσιν οἰκοδομήθη ὁ ναὸς οὗτος, καὶ σὺ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερεῖς αὐτόν;
2:20.targetText: “This temple took forty-six years to build,” the Jews replied, “and You are going to raise it up in three days?”

groups.note: Τεσσεράκοντα καὶ ἕξ ("forty and six") is rendered forty-six.
The passive οἰκοδομήθη ("was built") with the dative of time is rendered took … years to build.
The future ἐγερεῖς ("You will raise") is rendered are going to raise up.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:21.sourceText: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ἔλεγεν περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ.
2:21.targetText: But Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body.

groups.note: The demonstrative ἐκεῖνος ("that one") is rendered by the name Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:22.sourceText: ὅτε οὖν ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τοῦτο ἔλεγεν, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν τῇ γραφῇ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
2:22.targetText: After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:23.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἦν ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῷ πάσχα ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, θεωροῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει·
2:23.targetText: While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover Feast, many people saw the signs He was doing and believed in His name.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB joins ἐν τῷ πάσχα ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ ("at the Passover, at the feast") into one phrase, so the second ἐν and its article are not repeated.
BSB leaves αὐτοῦ ("his") unexpressed; He was doing shows whose signs they were.
BSB omits the relative pronoun ἅ ("which").

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle θεωροῦντες is rendered as the finite verb saw.

2:24.sourceText: αὐτὸς δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἐπίστευεν αὑτὸν αὐτοῖς διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν γινώσκειν πάντας,
2:24.targetText: But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all.

groups.note: διὰ τό with the infinitive ("because of His knowing") is rendered for.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the intensive αὐτός ("himself") with Jesus untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; πάντας means "all people".

2:25.sourceText: καὶ ὅτι οὐ χρείαν εἶχεν ἵνα τις μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου· αὐτὸς γὰρ ἐγίνωσκεν τί ἦν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ.
2:25.targetText: He did not need any testimony about man, for He knew what was in a man.

groups.note: χρείαν εἶχεν ("had need") is rendered did need.
The verb μαρτυρήσῃ ("should testify") is rendered by the noun testimony.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καὶ ὅτι ("and because"), which continues the reason from 2:24, unexpressed.
BSB renders the ἵνα clause ("that anyone should testify") as a noun phrase.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
